rationale: Measuring the automatic cadence, the last open point in the asserted defect's consequence. The harness now sets SnapshotInterval to 100ms instead of an hour and, after driving the node to the emptied state, samples the stored-snapshot count, snapshot index, applied index and shouldSnapshot every 200ms for about 1.2s, so the automatic runSnapshots path rather than direct takeSnapshot calls does the work. Native construction feedback with these fixed inputs produced a result that narrows my earlier phrasing: the stored count rose from 1 to 2 by 201ms and to 3 by 402ms, but then stayed at 3 for the remaining four samples out to 1207ms while shouldSnapshot stayed true with snapshot_index and applied_index unchanged at 3. So the automatic path did add redundant snapshots at the unchanged index, but it did not keep adding one per interval in this observation window; the plateau is not explained by this run, and candidate causes (snapshot-store retention, or a later takeSnapshot error that runSnapshots logs rather than returns) were not captured by the observations. I am submitting this as the fixed experiment for controller execution and flagging explicitly that the earlier limitation wording 'schedules a snapshot at the unchanged index on each interval' is now in question and must be narrowed to what the receipt shows.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold=10000 and SnapshotInterval=100ms. After the node becomes leader one command is applied and a user Snapshot() is run, and store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot are recorded. Six samples are then taken 200ms apart, each recording elapsed time, store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot, so any growth in the count is attributable to the node's own snapshot loop while no client command is applied.

experiment.prefix: inmemConfig supplies the defaults; TrailingLogs=0 makes the user snapshot's compaction trim up to the snapshot index and the large threshold makes the pre-state verdict false, while the 100ms interval makes the automatic loop fire several times inside the sampling window. MakeCluster(1, t, conf) starts the real node over InmemTransport with InmemStore logs and stable state and the cluster helper's in-memory snapshot store; the test waits for Leader before applying. No client command is issued after the emptied state, so the applied index is a constant control: any change in the stored-snapshot count while the applied index stays fixed comes from the node's own snapshot scheduling. All operands are package-internal reads of the runtime object plus the snapshot store's List(); no production logic is modified.
experiment.revision_reason: The previous execution triggered the snapshot path directly and could not speak to the cadence; this revision shortens SnapshotInterval to 100ms and samples over time so the automatic runSnapshots loop, not the harness, decides when snapshots are taken.
